question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Any female animal which feeds its young on milk from her own body
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Mammal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Mammal" is any warm-blooded vertebrate animal that feeds its young on milk secreted by mammary glands in the mother's own body, and is typically covered with hair. (स्तनधारी प्राणी)
◦ Example: Humans, dogs, whales and bats are all examples of mammals.

• The word is derived from the Latin "mamma", meaning "breast", referring to the mammary glands that produce milk.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Vertebrate (कशेरुकी प्राणी): Any animal possessing a backbone or spinal column; this is a broader category that includes mammals as well as fish, birds, reptiles and amphibians, so it does not specifically denote a milk-producing animal.

• Option 2: Parasite (परजीवी): An organism that lives in or on another organism (the host) and derives nutrients at the host's expense.

• Option 4: Fauna (प्राणी-जगत): The entire animal life of a particular region or period, taken collectively — not a single animal.

NOTE

• Other one-word substitutes for animal groups often asked in SSC: Carnivore (a flesh-eating animal), Herbivore (a plant-eating animal), Omnivore (an animal that eats both plants and flesh), and Nocturnal (an animal active at night).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Certain to happen
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Inevitable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inevitable" means certain to happen; unable to be avoided or prevented. (अवश्यंभावी / टलने योग्य नहीं)
◦ Example: Given the heavy rain, a delay in the flight's departure was inevitable.

• The word comes from the Latin "inevitabilis" (in- "not" + evitabilis "avoidable"), literally meaning "that cannot be avoided".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Justifiable (न्यायसंगत): Able to be shown to be right or reasonable.

• Option 2: Indispensable (अपरिहार्य): Absolutely necessary; too important to be without.

• Option 3: Convertible (परिवर्तनीय): Able to be changed or exchanged for something else in form or value.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "Inevitable" with "Indispensable" — the former relates to certainty of occurrence, the latter to necessity/importance.

• Other one-word substitutes for certainty: "Unavoidable" (cannot be avoided), "Imminent" (about to happen).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Nefew.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word is incorrectly spelt as "Nefew"; the correct spelling is "Nephew" — the son of one's brother or sister, or the son of one's brother-in-law or sister-in-law.

• Spelling key: N + E + PH + E + W. The middle sound is spelt with "ph" (not "f"), even though it is pronounced like an "f".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Father" is correctly spelt.

• Option 3: "Niece" is correctly spelt — the daughter of one's brother or sister.

• Option 4: "Uncle" is correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Other common words where "ph" is wrongly replaced with "f" by candidates: "Phase", "Physician", "Phenomenon", "Orphan", "Sphere".

• Related family-relation words often confused: Nephew (भतीजा/भांजा) vs Niece (भतीजी/भांजी).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Indolent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Active.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Indolent" means lazy; disliking physical activity or effort; averse to exertion. (आलसी)
◦ Example: The indolent student never completed his assignments on time.

• Its antonym is "Active", meaning energetic, diligent, and willing to work or move. (सक्रिय / फुर्तीला)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Lazy" is a synonym of "Indolent", not its antonym.

• Option 2: "Unskilled" means lacking skill or training; it is unrelated to laziness and is neither a synonym nor a true antonym of "Indolent".

• Option 4: "Sluggish" means slow-moving and lacking energy; it is also a synonym of "Indolent", not its antonym.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "Indolent": Lethargic, Idle, Slothful, Languid.

• Other antonyms of "Indolent": Diligent, Industrious, Energetic, Hardworking.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The Indian independence movement sought to establish the conceptions of freedom and social welfare as the goals of an independent Indian state, resulting in Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. concepts of liberty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined phrase "conceptions of freedom" means ideas or notions relating to liberty. (स्वतंत्रता की अवधारणाएँ)

• "Concepts of liberty" carries the exact same meaning — "concepts" is a direct synonym of "conceptions" (both mean ideas/notions), and "liberty" is a direct synonym of "freedom".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "procedures of free mind" is incorrect because "procedures" means set methods or processes, which does not match the meaning of "conceptions" (ideas), and "free mind" distorts the meaning of "freedom" as a political/social state.

• Option 3: "symbols of victory" is incorrect because neither "symbols" nor "victory" relates to the meaning of "conceptions of freedom"; this changes the meaning entirely.

• Option 4: "methods to sympathise" is incorrect because "methods to sympathise" (ways of showing sympathy) has no relation to ideas about freedom.

NOTE

• "Conception" (an idea/notion) should not be confused with "Perception" (the way something is understood/interpreted) or "Deception" (the act of deceiving).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
She might have completed her research by that time.
option_1: Her research might be completed by her by that time.
option_2: Her research might had been completed by her by that time.
option_3: Her research might have been completed by her by that time.
option_4: Her research might have completed by her by that time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Her research might have been completed by her by that time.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "She might have completed her research by that time" is in the Modal Perfect (might + have + V3) structure, used to express a past possibility.

• Rule — Passive voice with modal perfect (might/could/should/would + have + V3):
◦ Active: Subject + modal + have + V3 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + modal + have + been + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "her research" becomes the subject; the modal "might" is retained; "have" is followed by "been"; the main verb "completed" (already V3) is retained; and "she" becomes the agent "by her".
◦ Passive: Her research might have been completed by her by that time.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "might be completed" is the passive form of the Simple Present modal structure (might + V1), not the modal perfect (might + have + V3) of the original sentence.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "might had been completed" is grammatically wrong — after the modal "might", the auxiliary must be the bare form "have", never "had".

• Option 4 is incorrect because "might have completed" omits the auxiliary "been", which is compulsory to form the passive of a perfect structure.

NOTE

• The passive of a perfect modal always needs the pattern modal + have + been + V3; never drop "been" and never change "have" to "had" after a modal.

• Similar structures: could have been done, should have been finished, would have been written.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The police were on high alert on account of the _________ convict who had killed many people.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. runaway.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Runaway" (used here as an adjective before a noun) means having escaped, fled, or fugitive. (भगोड़ा)
◦ Example: The police launched a manhunt for the runaway prisoner.

• A "runaway convict" is a standard collocation meaning a convicted criminal who has escaped from custody — exactly the sense required by the sentence, which describes a convict the police were on alert for because he had killed many people (i.e., he was on the loose).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "run after" means to chase or pursue someone; it is a verb phrase and cannot grammatically function as an adjective before "convict".

• Option 2: "walk away" means to leave a place or situation, typically without much concern; it is a verb phrase and does not fit as an adjective modifying "convict".

• Option 3: "eloped" means to run away secretly to get married, and is used specifically in the context of marriage/romantic relationships; it does not fit the context of a dangerous convict and cannot be used adjectivally before a noun in this way.

NOTE

• "Runaway" can function as a noun (a person who has fled) as well as an adjective (a runaway train, a runaway convict, a runaway bride).

• Do not confuse "runaway" (escaped/fugitive) with "eloped" (specifically fleeing to marry secretly).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
He regards himself as a patriot.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. traitor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "patriot" means a person who loves, supports, and is loyal to their country. (देशभक्त)

• Its antonym is "traitor", meaning a person who betrays their country, a cause, or another person's trust. (देशद्रोही / गद्दार)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "nationalist" means a person with strong beliefs about the independence or interests of their nation; it is close in meaning to "patriot", not its opposite.

• Option 2: "dutiful" means conscientious and obedient in performing one's duties; it does not form a meaningful antonym pair with "patriot".

• Option 4: "loyal" means faithful and devoted; this is a synonym of the qualities of a "patriot", not its antonym.

NOTE

• Related word pair: Patriotism (देशभक्ति, love for one's country) is opposite to Treachery/Treason (देशद्रोह, betrayal of one's country).

• Do not confuse "traitor" (देशद्रोही) with "tyrant" (a cruel/oppressive ruler, अत्याचारी शासक).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
Lucy presented a lucid account of her achievements before the committee.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ambiguous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "lucid" means clearly expressed, easily understood; transparent in meaning. (स्पष्ट)

• Its antonym is "ambiguous", meaning open to more than one interpretation; not clearly expressed or understood. (अस्पष्ट / द्विअर्थी)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "orderly" means arranged in a neat, systematic way; it is not the opposite of "clear in meaning" and does not fit as an antonym of "lucid".

• Option 3: "intelligible" means able to be understood; it is a synonym of "lucid", not its antonym.

• Option 4: "transparent" means easy to understand or perceive; it is also a synonym of "lucid", not its antonym.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "lucid": Clear, Coherent, Comprehensible, Plain.

• Other antonyms of "lucid": Vague, Obscure, Confusing, Unclear.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Scrape the barrel
option_3: Using all the ways to achieve the desired result
option_4: To be forced to use one's last and weakest resource
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To be forced to use one's last and weakest resource.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Scrape the barrel" (fully, "to scrape the bottom of the barrel") means to be forced to use whatever remains, even if it is of the poorest quality, because nothing better is available. (जो कुछ बचा है उसी से काम चलाना, अंतिम व सबसे घटिया साधन का प्रयोग करना)
◦ Example: With so many players injured, the coach really had to scrape the barrel to field a full team.

• The idiom evokes the image of literally scraping the inside bottom of an empty barrel to collect the last, poorest-quality remnants of its contents (e.g., flour or salted meat) once the good stock is used up.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Trying to find something" is too general and does not capture the sense of "last resort/inferior quality" central to the idiom.

• Option 2: "Hiding something" is unrelated to the idiom's actual meaning.

• Option 3: "Using all the ways to achieve the desired result" describes resourcefulness in general, which is different from being forced to settle for an inferior, last-resort option.

NOTE

• Related idioms of scarcity/last resort often asked in SSC: "At the end of one's tether" (to have no strength or patience left), "On its last legs" (about to fail or collapse), and "A drop in the ocean" (an amount too small to make a difference).

question:
Select the sentence that uses the given idiom correctly.
A dime a dozen
option_1: Her ideas were worth a dime a dozen and didn't impress the boss.
option_2: The concert tickets were a dime a dozen and sold out quickly.
option_3: The restaurant had some delicious desserts that were a dime a dozen.
option_4: The antique store had some rare finds, but they were a dime a dozen.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Her ideas were worth a dime a dozen and didn't impress the boss.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "A dime a dozen" means very common and of little value or special worth; easily available in large numbers. (बहुत साधारण, आसानी से उपलब्ध, कम मूल्य का)
◦ Example: Smartphones are a dime a dozen these days, so it's hard for any one brand to stand out.

• In Option 1, the sentence correctly uses the idiom to say her ideas were unremarkable/commonplace, which logically explains why they "didn't impress the boss" — a common, unoriginal thing failing to impress makes complete sense.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is incorrect because if the tickets were "a dime a dozen" (common, easily available, low in value), they would logically NOT "sell out quickly" — items that sell out fast are typically scarce/in demand, which contradicts the idiom's meaning.

• Option 3 is incorrect because calling the desserts "delicious" and then saying they were "a dime a dozen" is contradictory — something described as delicious/special is not "common and unremarkable".

• Option 4 is incorrect because it directly contradicts itself: "rare finds" cannot logically also be "a dime a dozen" (common/unremarkable) — rare and common are opposites.

NOTE

• Other idioms of commonness/abundance: "Two a penny" (British equivalent of "a dime a dozen"), "Ten a penny", "Thick on the ground" (plentiful).

• Idioms of rarity (opposite sense): "Once in a blue moon", "Few and far between".

question: Identify the sentence that correctly uses the indefinite article.
option_1: She is a Indian artist married to an European engineer.
option_2: She is an Indian artist married to an European engineer.
option_3: She is an Indian artist married to a European engineer.
option_4: She is a Indian artist married to a European engineer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. She is an Indian artist married to a European engineer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule — Choice of indefinite article "a"/"an": The choice depends on the sound with which the following word begins, not merely its first letter.
◦ "An" is used before a word beginning with a vowel sound.
◦ "A" is used before a word beginning with a consonant sound.

• "Indian" begins with the vowel sound /ɪ/, so it takes "an" → "an Indian artist".

• "European" begins with the consonant (semi-vowel) sound /j/ (as in "yes"), even though it is spelt with the vowel letter "E", so it takes "a" → "a European engineer".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "a Indian" is incorrect because "Indian" begins with a vowel sound and must take "an".

• Option 2: "an Indian ... an European" is incorrect because although "an Indian" is correct, "European" begins with the consonant sound /j/ and must take "a", not "an".

• Option 4: "a Indian ... a European" is incorrect because "Indian" is wrongly given "a" instead of "an", even though "a European" is correct.

NOTE

• Other words starting with a vowel letter but a consonant sound (take "a"): University, Union, Uniform, Useful, One-eyed, European.

• Other words starting with a consonant letter but a vowel sound (take "an"): Hour, Honest, Honour, MBA, X-ray.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Wilfull.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word is incorrectly spelt as "Wilfull"; the correct spelling is "Wilful" (British English) or "Willful" (American English) — meaning done deliberately or on purpose, or stubbornly determined to do as one wants.

• Spelling key: the word takes only one final "l" — "Wil(l)-ful", never a double "l" at the end ("-full").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Fruitful" is correctly spelt — meaning producing good or plentiful results.

• Option 2: "Unction" is correctly spelt — meaning the act of anointing with oil, or excessive politeness/flattery.

• Option 4: "Cradle" is correctly spelt — meaning a baby's bed.

NOTE

• Words ending in "-ful" (never "-full") when used as a suffix: Beautiful, Careful, Useful, Faithful, Grateful, Wonderful.

• The word "full" itself is spelt with a double "l" only when standing alone or at the start of a compound (e.g., "full moon", "full-time").

question:
Select the word which means the same as the group of words underlined in the sentence.
Only the artists who make sculptures are allowed to take part in exhibitions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Sculptor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined group of words "the artists who make sculptures" is precisely defined by the single word "Sculptor" — an artist who creates three-dimensional works of art (sculptures) by carving, moulding, or casting materials such as stone, wood, clay, or metal. (मूर्तिकार)
◦ Example: Michelangelo was a renowned sculptor famous for his statue of David.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Painter" (चित्रकार): An artist who creates pictures using paint — a different art form (two-dimensional, not sculpture).

• Option 2: "Artisan" (शिल्पकार): A skilled worker who makes things by hand, especially in a traditional craft or trade; this is a broader, more general term and not specific to sculpture-making.

• Option 4: "Potter" (कुम्हार): A person who makes pottery — specifically vessels and objects from clay, shaped and fired, which is a distinct craft from sculpture.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes for artists/craftspeople: Calligrapher (one skilled in decorative handwriting), Weaver (one who weaves cloth), Architect (one who designs buildings).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Payments can be made by _________ or in cash.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. cheque.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cheque" is a written, dated, and signed instrument directing a bank to pay a specific sum of money to the bearer or a named person. (चेक, बैंक से भुगतान का आदेश-पत्र)
◦ Example: He paid the school fees by cheque instead of carrying cash.

• The sentence requires a mode/method of payment (parallel with "or in cash"), and "cheque" is the only option among the four that names a payment instrument.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "chick" means a young bird, especially a baby chicken; it is unrelated to payment.

• Option 2: "cheek" means the side of the face below the eye, or (informally) impudence; it is unrelated to payment.

• Option 4: "cheeky" is an adjective meaning impudent or disrespectful in a light-hearted way; it cannot function as a noun for a payment method and does not fit grammatically after "by".

NOTE

• "Cheque", "cheek" and "chick" are commonly confused in spelling-based SSC questions because of their similar sound/spelling — always check which one fits the meaning of the sentence.

• American English spells it "check" for the banking instrument, while British/Indian English uses "cheque".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word in the following sentence.
Traitor
People should vote for honest and loyal leaders not for betrayer and defender.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Loyal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given word "Traitor" means a person who betrays their country, a cause, a principle, or another person's trust; one who is disloyal. (देशद्रोही / विश्वासघाती)

• Its antonym is "Loyal", meaning faithful and steadfast in allegiance to a person, cause, or country. (वफादार)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Honest" means truthful and sincere; while a positive trait, it is not specifically the opposite of "Traitor" (which concerns betrayal of allegiance, not truthfulness).

• Option 2: "Defender" means a person who protects or guards something; this is close in spirit to loyalty but is not as precise or direct an antonym as "Loyal", and does not form a standard antonym pair with "Traitor".

• Option 3: "Betrayer" means one who betrays trust or is unfaithful; this is essentially a synonym of "Traitor", not its antonym.

NOTE

• Related word pairs: Loyalty ↔ Treachery/Treason, Patriot ↔ Traitor, Ally ↔ Betrayer.

• Do not confuse "Traitor" (one who betrays) with "Tyrant" (a cruel ruler) or "Trader" (one who buys/sells goods) — these are frequently confused due to similar spelling.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
She always / invite me / to / dinner.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. invite me.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "She", a third-person singular subject.

• Rule — Simple Present Tense with third-person singular subject: When the subject is he/she/it or any singular noun, the main verb must take an -s/-es ending (i.e., the V5 form) in the simple present tense.

• The segment "invite me" wrongly uses the base form "invite" instead of the correct third-person singular form "invites". The sentence should read: "She always invites me to dinner."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "She always" is correct — a valid subject with the frequency adverb "always" correctly placed before the main verb.

• Option 2: "to" is correct — the preposition "to" correctly precedes the destination/purpose "dinner".

• Option 3: "dinner" is correct — a valid noun completing the sentence with no error.

NOTE

• Frequency adverbs like always, often, usually, sometimes, never are placed before the main verb but after the auxiliary/"to be" verb.

• Common subject-verb agreement error pattern in SSC: singular subject (he/she/it/singular noun) + base verb without "-s/-es" is always an error in the simple present tense.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
By whom was the coffee made?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Who made the coffee?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "By whom was the coffee made?" is a passive interrogative sentence in the Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Active voice of a passive question with "by whom": When a passive question begins with "By whom + was/were + Subject + V3?", the active voice is formed as "Who + V2 + Object?" — the agent "by whom" becomes the interrogative subject "Who".
◦ Passive: By whom + was/were + Object + V3?
◦ Active: Who + V2 (past tense) + Object?

• Applying the rule: "was made" (passive, past) becomes "made" (V2, active past tense), "the coffee" (the passive subject) becomes the object, and "by whom" becomes the active subject "Who".
◦ Active: Who made the coffee?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Who had made the coffee?" is incorrect because "had made" is the Past Perfect Tense, which does not match the Simple Past Tense of the given passive sentence.

• Option 3: "Who has made the coffee?" is incorrect because "has made" is the Present Perfect Tense, which does not match the Simple Past Tense of the original.

• Option 4: "Who makes the coffee?" is incorrect because "makes" is the Simple Present Tense, which does not match the Simple Past Tense ("was made") of the given sentence.

NOTE

• When converting a passive question with "by whom" to active voice, always retain the same tense as the original passive sentence — only the subject/agent position and verb form change.

• Compare: Passive "By whom is the coffee made?" (Present) → Active "Who makes the coffee?".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined words in the given sentence.
Developed countries are at a disadvantage to have access to modern science and technologies.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. privileged.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined phrase "at a disadvantage" means in an unfavourable position; lacking the resources, opportunities, or conditions that others have. (प्रतिकूल स्थिति में / नुकसान की स्थिति में)

• Its antonym is "privileged", meaning having special rights, advantages, or opportunities that others do not have. (विशेषाधिकार प्राप्त / लाभप्रद स्थिति में)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "powered" means supplied with energy or force to operate; it does not form a meaningful antonym pair with "at a disadvantage".

• Option 3: "useless" means having no purpose or function; this does not describe a favourable position and is unrelated to the sense of "advantage".

• Option 4: "unhappy" relates to emotional state, not to relative advantage/disadvantage, so it is not the correct antonym here.

NOTE

• Related word pair: Advantage/Advantaged ↔ Disadvantage/Disadvantaged; Privileged ↔ Underprivileged.

• "At a disadvantage" is a fixed prepositional phrase; its natural single-word antonym is best expressed by "privileged" or "advantaged".

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. According to Homer, Achilles was brought up by his mother at Phthia with his inseparable companion Patroclus.
B. Achilles was the bravest, handsomest and greatest warrior of the army of Agamemnon in the Trojan War.
C. Later non-Homeric tales suggest that Patroclus was Achilles' kinsman or lover.
D. Achilles, in Greek mythology, is the son of the mortal Peleus, king of the Myrmidons, and the Nereid Thetis.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. DBAC.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence D — "Achilles, in Greek mythology, is the son of the mortal Peleus, king of the Myrmidons, and the Nereid Thetis" — introduces the subject "Achilles" for the very first time with his parentage, so it must be the opening sentence.

• Sentence B — "Achilles was the bravest, handsomest and greatest warrior of the army of Agamemnon in the Trojan War" — logically follows D by describing Achilles' stature/role as a warrior, continuing directly from the introduction.

• Sentence A — "According to Homer, Achilles was brought up by his mother at Phthia with his inseparable companion Patroclus" — follows B, moving to details of his upbringing and introduces "Patroclus", a new name.

• Sentence C — "Later non-Homeric tales suggest that Patroclus was Achilles' kinsman or lover" — must come last, since it elaborates further ("Later...tales suggest") on Patroclus, who was only just introduced in sentence A.

• This gives the coherent, chronological, and logically linked order: D–B–A–C.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (ABCD) is incorrect because it opens with sentence A, which uses the pronoun-like reference "his mother" without having first established who "Achilles" is — B and D must precede it.

• Option 3 (DABC) is incorrect because it places A (upbringing, introducing Patroclus) before B (his general stature as a warrior); logically, Achilles' identity/status as the great warrior (B) should be established right after his parentage (D), before the narrative moves on to his upbringing (A).

• Option 4 (CABD) is incorrect because it begins with C, which refers to "Patroclus" and uses "Later...tales suggest" — a phrase that only makes sense after Patroclus has already been introduced, so C cannot be the opening sentence.

NOTE

• In para-jumble/sentence-rearrangement questions, always look for the sentence that introduces the main subject by name (here, "Achilles" in D) to identify the likely opening line, and track pronouns/new names (like "Patroclus") to fix the logical sequence.

• Phrases like "Later...", "However,", and "This..." are strong clues that a sentence cannot be the first in the sequence.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Ambition is a vital ingredient for success. Without ambition to push us, we will not be (1)________ of great achievements. We all need that special something (2)________ ourselves to give us the willpower to reach a higher goal (3)________ we imagine ourselves capable (4)________.
Yet, ambition, (5)________ money and fire, is a good servant, but a bad master.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. capable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a word that logically completes **"we will not be (1)________ of great achievements" — the fixed collocation is "capable of"**, meaning having the ability or capacity to do something.

• "Capable" fits perfectly: "we will not be capable of great achievements" = we will not have the ability to achieve great things.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "able" is close in meaning but does not fit idiomatically with the preposition "of" followed by a noun phrase in this construction as naturally as "capable of" does; "capable of" is the standard fixed collocation used with nouns describing ability/potential in this context.

• Option 3: "durable" means able to withstand wear; it makes no sense with achievements.

• Option 4: "curable" means able to be cured (of a disease); it is completely unrelated to the context of achievement.

NOTE

• Fixed collocation: "capable of" + noun/gerund (e.g., capable of hard work, capable of winning).

• Do not confuse "capable" (having ability) with "able" (usually followed by "to + verb", as in "able to achieve"), "durable" (long-lasting), and "curable" (treatable).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Ambition is a vital ingredient for success. Without ambition to push us, we will not be (1)________ of great achievements. We all need that special something (2)________ ourselves to give us the willpower to reach a higher goal (3)________ we imagine ourselves capable (4)________.
Yet, ambition, (5)________ money and fire, is a good servant, but a bad master.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. within.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a preposition that logically completes **"that special something (2)________ ourselves"** — the passage is describing an inner drive or quality that exists inside a person.

• "Within" means inside; contained in the limits of — so "that special something within ourselves" correctly conveys an inner quality/drive that resides inside a person.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "in" could loosely suggest location but does not carry the same sense of "deep inside/inherent to" that the context demands as precisely as "within" does; "within ourselves" is the standard, idiomatic phrase for an inner quality.

• Option 2: "with" means accompanied by or by means of; "that special something with ourselves" is not idiomatic and does not convey the intended meaning of an inner drive.

• Option 3: "without" means outside of or lacking; this would reverse the intended meaning, suggesting the special something is external or absent, which contradicts the passage's meaning.

NOTE

• "Within" is commonly used in expressions describing inner qualities or limits: within oneself, within reach, within limits, within reason.

• Do not confuse "within" (inside) with "without" (outside/lacking), which are opposites.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Ambition is a vital ingredient for success. Without ambition to push us, we will not be (1)________ of great achievements. We all need that special something (2)________ ourselves to give us the willpower to reach a higher goal (3)________ we imagine ourselves capable (4)________.
Yet, ambition, (5)________ money and fire, is a good servant, but a bad master.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. than.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows a comparative construction: **"to reach a higher goal (3)________ we imagine ourselves capable of" — the word "higher" is a comparative adjective, and comparative adjectives are always followed by "than"**.

• Rule: Comparative adjective/adverb + "than" is the standard grammatical pattern for comparison in English.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "then" is an adverb of time/sequence (meaning "at that time" or "next"); it is a common error to confuse it with "than" (used for comparison), but it does not fit grammatically after the comparative "higher".

• Option 3: "that" is used as a conjunction, relative pronoun, or demonstrative, but it cannot follow a comparative adjective like "higher" to introduce a comparison.

• Option 4: "what" is an interrogative/relative pronoun and does not fit grammatically after a comparative adjective in this construction.

NOTE

• "Than" vs "Then" is one of the most common confusion pairs in SSC exams: "than" is used only for comparison (taller than, better than, higher than); "then" relates to time or sequence (first this, then that).

• Other comparative structures: more...than, less...than, better...than, worse...than.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Ambition is a vital ingredient for success. Without ambition to push us, we will not be (1)________ of great achievements. We all need that special something (2)________ ourselves to give us the willpower to reach a higher goal (3)________ we imagine ourselves capable (4)________.
Yet, ambition, (5)________ money and fire, is a good servant, but a bad master.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank completes the fixed phrase **"we imagine ourselves capable (4)________", which requires the preposition "of" to complete the standard collocation "capable of"**.

• Rule: The adjective "capable" is always followed by the preposition "of" (never "about", "off", or "on") when it precedes a noun or gerund describing what someone is able to do.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "about" does not form a correct collocation with "capable"; the correct fixed phrase is "capable of", not "capable about".

• Option 2: "off" does not fit grammatically or idiomatically after "capable"; it also creates confusion with the similarly spelt correct preposition "of".

• Option 4: "on" does not form a correct collocation with "capable"; "capable on" is not standard English usage.

NOTE

• Reinforces the same rule tested in Q.21/blank (1): "capable of" is a fixed, non-negotiable collocation in English.

• Commonly confused preposition pair in spelling/sound: "of" (belonging to/preposition of possession or relation) vs. "off" (away from/preposition of separation) — candidates often mix these up.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Ambition is a vital ingredient for success. Without ambition to push us, we will not be (1)________ of great achievements. We all need that special something (2)________ ourselves to give us the willpower to reach a higher goal (3)________ we imagine ourselves capable (4)________.
Yet, ambition, (5)________ money and fire, is a good servant, but a bad master.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. like.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a word that introduces a comparison in the sentence **"Yet, ambition, (5)________ money and fire, is a good servant, but a bad master"** — ambition is being compared to money and fire as things that serve the same dual nature (useful if controlled, dangerous if not).

• "Like" used as a preposition means "similar to; in the same way as", and is the standard word used to introduce such a comparison between nouns.
◦ Example: Fire, like ambition, can be a helpful servant or a destructive master depending on how it is controlled.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "as" is typically used to describe a role/function ("as a servant") or in clauses of comparison with a verb ("as they say"), not to directly compare two nouns in this position; "like" is the natural choice for comparing "ambition" with "money and fire" as nouns.

• Option 3: "such" would require the correlative structure "such...as" (e.g., "such things as money and fire") and cannot stand alone in this position to mean "similar to".

• Option 4: "similarly" is an adverb typically used to begin or link independent clauses/sentences (e.g., "Similarly, fire can be dangerous"), not to directly compare two noun phrases within a single clause as required here.

NOTE

• "Like" (preposition, comparing nouns) vs "As" (conjunction/preposition of role, e.g., "he works as a teacher", or introducing a clause, "as I said before") is a classic SSC distinction.

• The sentence expresses a well-known saying pattern: "X is a good servant but a bad master", commonly applied to fire, money, and ambition — meaning these things are beneficial when controlled but harmful when they control us.
